name: OPA1688 / OPA1689 (TI SoundPlus OPA168x: 36 V, 10 MHz CMOS audio op-amp with a rail-to-rail high-drive output; dual / quad)
tagline: Cheap, rugged 36 V TI SoundPlus CMOS dual with a rail-to-rail high-drive output. A diyAudio member called it 'a 21st-century NE5532'.
technology: CMOS-input SoundPlus audio op-amp (input bias ±10 pA typ). Runs from 4.5 V (±2.25 V) to 36 V (±18 V), 10 MHz GBW, rail-to-rail output, marketed as 'Low Distortion High Drive'. SMD only. OPA1688 (dual) comes in SOIC-8 (D) and WSON-8 (DRG). OPA1689 (quad) comes in SOIC-14 and VQFN-16, per distributor listings.

reputation.summary: It is not a socket-rolling legend because it is SMD-only. It is well regarded as an inexpensive, rugged all-rounder. A diyAudio member called it 'a very good all-round opamp at a reasonable price, like a 21st century version of the NE5532', with modest 8 nV/√Hz noise. Builders value its 36 V operation, rail-to-rail high-drive output and short-circuit protection, which let it drive headphones directly. One GitHub modder reports it as the final stage of the Topping NX4 DSD, and built an adapter to swap in the INA1620. Other reported uses include DIY headphone amps (HiFiVision build, diyAudio OPA1688/OPA1622 thread), DJ-mixer cue outputs, DAC reconstruction filters and retro-computer audio boards. Forum threads (TI E2E, AudioKarma, Head-Fi) suggest it as an SMD substitute for the discontinued OPA2604AP. TI's own 'next-generation OPA2134/OPA2604 replacement' FAQ is about the OPA1656. No Audio Science Review or Samuel Groner measurements were found.
typical_uses: Headphone driver / output stage (Topping NX4 DSD final stage per one modder; HiFiVision DIY headphone amp; DJ mixer cue output)
Line-level buffers, line-level converters and headphone pre-amps (synth DIY)
DAC output / reconstruction filter (FPGA sigma-delta DAC project)
SMD substitute for OPA2604 / OPA2134 in new designs
Retro-computer and sound-card audio outputs (ZX-Evolution rev D+, Mac NuBus PAS16 daughterboard)
caveats: Voltage noise (8 nV/√Hz) is modest next to OPA1656 (2.9 nV/√Hz), OPA1612 or OPA1602. It is not ideal for low-level sources such as phono or microphone inputs.
SMD only: OPA1688 in SOIC-8 or WSON-8, OPA1689 in SOIC-14 or VQFN-16. There is no DIP version, so socket rolling needs an adapter (WSON is hard to adapt).

Output power into low-impedance headphones is limited. One design note found OPA1688 current insufficient for a 250 mW / 18 Ω target (AarnimM22/HD800-wireless), and Topping NX4 owners swapped in the INA1620 for more drive.
Little independent measurement coverage, so the praise rests mostly on specs and value.

revision_history.changes: Initial release, OPA1688 dual only (per the SBOS724A header 'SEPTEMBER 2015' and TI PSpice model headers).

The change log includes 'updated the numbering format for tables, figures, and cross-references throughout the document'. The datasheet was re-titled 'OPA168x' and now covers the quad OPA1689 (SOIC-14, VQFN-16). Whether any OPA1688 electrical limits changed was not retrieved. TI's PSpice model re-matched GBW and slew rate 'as per the datasheet' around the same time.

Confirmed from the current symlink PDF: the revision-history heading reads 'Changes from Revision * (September 2015) to Revision A', and the listed changes include 'Updated the numbering format for tables, figures, and cross-references throughout the document'. The full change list, including the OPA1689 addition and any OPA1688 limit changes, did not appear in the search summary.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remarking reports specific to the OPA1688 were found. It is SMD-only (SOIC-8 / WSON-8) and inexpensive, so it is a far less attractive target than the DIP parts it substitutes for (OPA2604AP, OPA2134PA), which are heavily faked. Marketplace risk still applies: Amazon lists '1PCS OPA1688IDRGR OPA1688IDRGT OPA1688 OP1688 WSON8' and 2025 Chinese BOMs source OPA1688IDR from Taobao. 'OP1688' may be the WSON top mark (unconfirmed). Buy from TI or authorized distributors. One third-party catalog lists 'OPA1688AIDR', which does not match TI orderables (OPA1688ID, IDR, IDRGR, IDRGT), so treat such strings with suspicion.

revision_chain_notes:
I used 4 of 4 WebSearch calls. TI is the only vendor. The TI SBOS724 chain has two known revisions, oldest to newest:

1. **SBOS724 (rev *), September 2015.** This is the original release, covering the OPA1688 dual only. No copy was found that the search summary confirms as rev *. My searches for the header 'SBOS724 – SEPTEMBER 2015' with no 'REVISED' returned only rev A copies. Some mirrors might hold the original edition, but none showed a header:
   - Alldatasheet 734408, already listed
   - Alldatasheet 785948 (new)
   - datasheetspdf.com OPA1688 page and pdf/1408408, which matches Datasheet4U id=1408408 (new)
   - AiPCBA (new)
   - RadioLocman di=305497, already listed

   The best way to recover rev * is the Wayback Machine, using two seeds:
   - The TI symlink http://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa1688.pdf, captured between September 2015 and May 2022. The symlink held rev * until June 2022.
   - The revision-specific path https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/sbos724/sbos724.pdf. I built this URL from TI's usual lit/ds/<docnum>/<docnum>.pdf pattern; no search result showed it.

2. **SBOS724A (rev A), revised June 2022.** This revision re-titled the datasheet OPA168x and added the quad OPA1689. It is confirmed at https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/sbos724a/sbos724a.pdf (new) and at the current symlink. Its revision-history heading, 'Changes from Revision * (September 2015) to Revision A', confirms there was no intermediate revision between * and A.

No revision after A (B or later) turned up as of September 2026. Still missing:
- A copy confirmed as holding rev *
- Rev *'s full electrical tables, needed to check whether the OPA1688 limits or characteristics changed in rev A
- The full rev A change list

There are no second sources, acquirer re-issues or other vendor editions.
